hero.lead: An open-source community for developers who care about in-depth, expert-reviewed content.

about.title: About FullstacksJS
about.content: <mark>FullstacksJS</mark> is an open-source community focused on knowledge sharing, exploring, and enhancing developer experience. The primary objective of this community is to establish a professional environment for in-depth contents in software development and engineering field. In order to learn and strengthen the culture of open source development and contribution, the projects that are developed in this community are entirely open source, and members are encouraged to participate.

motivation.title: Motivation
motivation.content: The Internet is full of unfiltered programming content, tutorials, and forums, which provide incomplete, outdated, and sometimes incorrect information to the knowledge seekers in this field. Therefore, we decided to establish a community where experts control and review the contents and activities. This creates a community that values in-depth and correct content.

values.title: Values
values.content: Values form our community and influence its behavior also have a direct impact on community's decision-making and contents.
values.ethics: Ethics: Ethics is the most important value in the community, which has the highest priority in decisions. In the community, moral principles are never sacrificed for the sake of other activities.
values.validity: Validity: Expert approval is required for every community-produced and published content. If an error is discovered in previously published content, the community must notify the appropriate parties and update the content.
values.professionalism: Professionalism: Beyond skills, it's professionalism that defines us

rules.title: FullstacksJS Rules
rules.desc: The following behaviors are considered harassment and are unacceptable within our community:

violence.title: Violence
violence.desc: Violence, threats of violence, or violent language directed against another person. This includes wishing harm on someone.

name-calling.title: Name-calling
name-calling.desc: Calling a person or a group of people offensive names, mocking who they are, or using degrading nicknames, even when you think it is friendly banter.

nsfw.title: NSFW
nsfw.desc: Posting NSFW material, sexually explicit or graphically violent images, links, or text. Including avatars and usernames.

personal.title: Sharing private information
personal.desc: Posting other people's personally identifying information: real names, addresses, phone numbers, workplaces, or private conversations and photos shared without their consent.

insult.title: Insults
insult.desc: Insults or hate speech based on gender, race, religion, disability, nationality, or sexual orientation.

sex.title: Unwelcome sexual attention
sex.desc: Sexual comments, jokes, advances, or repeated romantic interest that the other person has not invited. If someone asks you to stop, stop immediately.

copyright.title: Copyrighted content
copyright.desc: Posting or requesting content subject to copyright: pirated books and courses, cracked software, or leaked paid material.

spam.title: Spam and flooding
spam.desc: Spam or flooding: unsolicited advertising, referral links, self-promotion outside the channels meant for it, and repetitive messages that bury the conversation.

dm.title: Unsolicited direct messages
dm.desc: Do not direct message someone unless they've granted permission. Ask your question in the public channel first, the answer usually helps others too, and take no for an answer.

advocate.title: Advocating for the above
advocate.desc: Encouraging, defending, or organizing any of the behavior listed here is treated exactly the same as doing it yourself.

controversial.title: Controversial topics
controversial.desc: Discussions on controversial religious or political topics. They rarely end well in a technical community, so please keep them out of our channels.

disturb.title: Harassment and scams
disturb.desc: Attempts to send messages with the intent to blackmail, annoy, scam, or disturb others, in public channels.

kind.title: Be kind and courteous
kind.desc: Friendly and professional is the default tone here. There's no need to be mean or rude to make a point, and newcomers deserve extra patience.

topic.title: Post in the right topic
topic.desc: Every channel has a purpose. Starting a conversation in the wrong one makes it harder for people to follow along and harder for the next person to find the answer.

cross.title: Don't cross-post
cross.desc: Pick the single most relevant channel and ask there. Posting the same thing in multiple topics splits the answers and clutters the community.

opinion.title: Respect differences of opinion
opinion.desc: People come from different backgrounds and experiences. Argue with the idea and bring reasons for it, never attack the person holding it.

ask.title: How to ask a question
ask.intro: To get the best answers, ask questions in a way that makes it easy for others to understand your problem and provide help. Here are some tips to help you ask better questions.

precise.title: Be precise and informative about your problem
precise.desc: Rather than just saying "my code doesn't work" provide specific details about the issue you're facing. For example, mention the programming language you're using, any error messages you're receiving, and the steps you've taken so far to try and resolve the problem.

environment.title: Describe the environment in which it occurs
environment.desc: Mention the OS, runtime, or application you're using, along with any relevant settings or configurations.

diagnostic.title: Describe the diagnostic steps you took to try and pin down the problem yourself
diagnostic.desc: If you've tried any troubleshooting steps, such as testing different configurations or reinstalling software, mention what you did and what the results were.

sandbox.title: Where's the code?
sandbox.desc: If your question is related to a piece of code you've written, make sure to include that code in your post. But be mindful of the length of your code and use tools like codesandbox.com or stackblitz.com to share it more efficiently.

courteous.title: Be courteous
courteous.desc: Remember that people are taking time out of their day to help you, so be polite and respectful in your interactions with them.

topic.title: Choose the topic carefully
topic.desc: Make sure your post is categorized in a way that accurately reflects the topic you're asking about. This will help ensure that your question is seen by people who are knowledgeable about the subject matter.

xy.title: Describe the goal, not the step
xy.desc: Rather than just asking how to do something, describe the larger goal you're trying to achieve. This can help others provide more useful and relevant advice.

rush.title: Don't rush to claim that you have found a bug
rush.desc: Even if you're pretty sure that you've found a bug, it's best to approach the issue as if it might be something you're doing wrong. This can help ensure that you're open to suggestions and don't waste time chasing down a non-existent bug.

guess.title: Describe the problem's symptoms, not your guesses
guess.desc: Avoid making assumptions or speculating about the cause of the problem. Stick to describing the symptoms you're experiencing and let others help you diagnose the underlying issue.

pv.title: Don't ask people to reply by PV
pv.desc: Keep the conversation public so that others can benefit from the discussion and provide their own insights.

homework.title: Avoid posting homework questions
homework.desc: While it's okay to ask for hints or guidance, avoid asking for full solutions to homework problems. The point of homework is to learn, so take advantage of the opportunity to develop your skills by working through the problem on your own.

precise.bad: My code doesn't work. Please help.
precise.good: On Node 20, fetch() throws ECONNREFUSED when I call my local API. Here's the request and the full stack trace.

sandbox.bad: Pasting 300 lines of your whole project into the message.
sandbox.good: A minimal reproduction on StackBlitz with only the failing component, plus a link.

xy.bad: How do I force-push over my teammate's commits?
xy.good: I need my branch to match main without losing my two local commits, what's the safe way?

guess.bad: The router is definitely caching my route, how do I disable that?
guess.good: /profile shows the previous user's data until I hard-refresh. Here's what I see.

Ready to join the TypeScript Guild?

Here, we dive into the world of advanced TypeScript by solving daily code challenges, unleashing the full potential of this language.



Which challenges are we talking about? Well, there's an incredible GitHub Repository called Type Challenge, and as a guild, we will collaborate to conquer 100 challenges from there.



Join us if you are prepared to tackle challenging coding puzzles, master advanced concepts, and elevate your TypeScript skills alongside a community of enthusiasts.
